title: A clean image build of platform-k develop fails: services/governance does not compile (TS2742 on router's inferred type) — a new slot cannot start until the image exists from an older build
description:
## Seen (2026-09-29, develop `0aa9b52c6`; origin/develop `b4461d1e2` is three commits ahead, none touching governance)

Starting a fresh stack slot with no cached images (`Start_Up/start-secuura.sh` via platform-s's `up-slot.sh 4`) fails at the governance image:

```
docker compose -p secuura_slot4 build --progress=plain governance
#19 1.611 src/routes/governance.ts(19,7): error TS2742: The inferred type of 'router' cannot be
      named without a reference to '@secuura/shared/node_modules/@types/express-serve-static-core'.
      This is likely not portable. A type annotation is necessary.
#19 ERROR: process "/bin/sh -c npm run build" did not complete successfully: exit code: 1
```

Reproducible: the same `docker compose build governance` fails the same way on a second run. Slots 1–3 on this machine start only because they hold `secuura_slot{1,2,3}-governance` images built up to two weeks ago; slot 4 had no image and could not be built. A new developer machine, or a slot torn down with `--rmi all` (the test-discipline teardown), hits this.

The first attempt on the same slot failed one image earlier — `nft-certificate` at `npm ci --ignore-scripts` — and that one built cleanly on retry, so it was transient; governance is not.

## Suggested fix

`services/governance/src/routes/governance.ts:19` — give `router` an explicit type (`const router: Router = express.Router()`), the usual TS2742 remedy when a workspace package (`@secuura/shared`) carries its own `@types/express-serve-static-core`. Worth a `tsc --noEmit` over every service in the PR gate so a non-portable inferred type cannot land again.

## Impact on platform-s

Blocks pairing an S slot with a fresh K slot for the gate run on platform-s PR #889 (the S↔K remediation branch); recorded there and on [PS-928](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-928/k-live-goes-red-on-the-second-full-run-on-a-slot-the-anchor-refresher). Related: [KS-955](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-955/a-fresh-clone-cannot-run-the-four-platform-suites-and-fails-in-a-way) (a fresh clone cannot run the suites).

nodes.title: Refs KS-1387: the governance router carries an explicit Router type

nodes.body:
@kamil.kreiser — the rebuild evidence, as asked. Read it before deciding; on your own criterion it does **not** close this ticket.

- **Command:** `./Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --rebuild` (Stuart, by hand, from his `~/obd-dev/platform-k` clone, clean on `develop` at **`78cb3c393`**), slot 1, 2026-10-18 22:45:40Z → 23:02:58Z. The script builds **serially**, one `docker compose --progress=plain -f docker-compose.local.yml build <service>` per service with `COMPOSE_BAKE=0`; it passes **no `--no-cache`**, so the layer cache was warm from the 15 Oct build — not a cold build. `governance` built 22:53:14Z → 22:54:38Z (image `2f87233cfc20`), then the script went on to `issuer-frontend`; all 33 services came up healthy, `/health/deep` 200, migrations `applied=0 skipped=51`.
- **The variable you named:** inside `platform-k-governance:latest` there is exactly **one** copy of `@types/express-serve-static-core`, at `/shared/node_modules/…`, version **`4.19.9`** — no nested second copy. That is the repository-lockfile layout you describe as the one in which the pre-fix tip also builds clean.

So this build shows that develop at `78cb3c393` (which carries `b45b69171`) builds under the single-copy layout; it cannot distinguish "the explicit `Router` type removed the error class" from "this layout never produces it". The sentence in our document is corrected accordingly: fixed on develop, proven only in the non-reproducing layout. Leave the ticket where you judge it; nothing on S waits on it.

**BLUF: @stuart.jamieson — your document says this is fixed and proven by a clean rebuild of develop on 19 Oct across 33 services, and asks us to close it. I am not closing it on that, and I would rather tell you exactly why than close it quietly. Could you paste the rebuild evidence here? Then it closes on your measurement rather than on nobody's.**

**Why your claim is not yet this ticket's evidence.** The ticket's acceptance is a clean *image* build of develop. The last work recorded here is explicit that the clean image build **was never run on our side** — the Docker daemon was down on the machine doing the work — and that is still true today: there is no Docker on the machine I am on, so I cannot reproduce your result or contradict it.

**And there is a reason not to assume it.** When the TS2742 failure was examined, it only reproduced when the two nested `@types/express-serve-static-core` copies were pinned to **different** versions. With the repository's own lockfiles both resolve to `4.19.9`, and in that layout **the pre-fix tip builds clean too**. So a green build of develop is consistent with two different worlds: the fix removed the error class, or the lockfile state was never going to produce it. A green build alone does not distinguish them, which means closing on "it builds now" could close a ticket whose symptom is still live for anyone whose install hoists differently.

**What would settle it,** and any one of these is enough:

1. The **exact command** you ran (`docker compose build`, a specific Dockerfile target, or something else) and **which develop SHA**.
2. Whether the 33 services were built **from a cold cache** — a warm layer cache can skip the compile step that fails.
3. If you have it, the resolved `@types/express-serve-static-core` versions in the image that built, since that is the variable the failure turns on.

Paste that and I will record it as the evidence and close the ticket against it. If you would rather not spend the time, say so and I will leave it In Progress with this comment as the reason — that is a better outcome than a ticket closed on an unverified claim.

No date, and nothing else is blocked on this.

**PR #1581 is merged to `develop` as `b45b69171b362da0233842cdd14c161c2f9266c2`.** `governance.ts:19` now reads `const router: Router = Router();`. Nothing deployed; the ticket stays In Progress.

**What gate H2 showed about TS2742 — stated exactly, because it decides whether this ticket's symptom is closed.** H2 reproduced TS2742 **without Docker**, but **only by pinning the two nested `@types/express-serve-static-core` copies to DIFFERENT versions**: in that layout the tip fails and this head builds clean, so **the change removes that error class**. **With the repository's real lockfiles both copies are `4.19.9` and the tip builds clean too.** So whether the ticket's original image-build failure is closed stays **"not reproduced with the real lockfiles"**. The clean `docker compose build governance` was not run (no Docker daemon in my environment) — that remains the real check, e.g. at the next governance deploy.

**Low note from H2:** the new `ks1387` suite goes red if a trailing comment is ever added to the declaration line (it matches the line literally).

**Evidence on the tree that landed** (predicted commit `4a87bcb052fa`, tree `f33b620c79e8` — byte-identical to the PR head's own tree, develop having not moved since the gate), in two environments: the new suite **3/3**; governance in full **119/119**; `tsc` (TypeScript 5.9.3) rc 0. Five-point read 5/5 TRUE.

**Raised as PR #1581**, head `6b4bcaec11fa4aea156a11bbaa23b56b09126b63`, on develop `385fc288fae8`. Not merged, not deployed.

`services/governance/src/routes/governance.ts:19` — `const router: Router = Router();`. Byte-checked: the applied file differs from the tip **only on that line** (the Spark patch's blank-line churn around it is a no-op; lines 18 and 20 are byte-identical).

**This ticket's own symptom is NOT reproduced, and I want that to be plain.** The clean image build was **not run** — the Docker daemon is down here. Governance's local `npm run build` is rc 0 **at the tip as well as with the change**, because this install hoists `@types/express-serve-static-core` to the root and has no copy nested under `packages/shared` — the layout that triggers TS2742. So a local pass is **not** evidence the image build is fixed. The real check is `docker compose build governance` from a clean cache; worth running at the next governance deploy.

Evidence (mine): red-first **2/1** (the annotation cell); green **3/3**; governance in full **119/119**; `tsc` rc 0; push preflight 13/16, nothing failed.

Clean build confirmed, 2 Oct. `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=3 ./Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --rebuild` at develop `88e8877a2`: **35 of 35 services built, 0 failed**, including `governance`, `analytics` and `billing`; the stack came up with 33 containers running (32 with a healthcheck, all healthy) and the two one-shot jobs (`migrations`, `demo-overlay`) exited 0; gateway `/health` and `/health/deep` both 200. The first pass was cut off by my session's time limit at service 32 during a slow package download, so the last four were built on a second pass with the first 31 from cache — no service failed in either pass.

The fault this ticket records is gone (fixed by KS-1380, `6cf5c3629`). Safe to close from the Platform-S side.

One thing worth knowing for slot users: before the rebuild, slot 3 started in under a minute on images dated 15 Sep while its owner marker read `develop @ 88e8877a2`. The marker records the checkout, not what the images were built from.

Re-read at develop `88e8877a2` (2 Oct): KS-1380's fix has merged (`6cf5c3629`), and `services/analytics`, `services/billing`, `services/governance` and `packages/shared` now all lock `@types/express-serve-static-core` 4.19.9 and `@types/pg` 8.23.1. That removes the cause recorded here. I have not re-run the clean image build, so this is from the lock files only; the ticket can close once one clean build of those three services is confirmed.

Definitive list, every service built one at a time from `0aa9b52c6` with Docker's disk cleared: **three fail** — `governance` (TS2742), `analytics` (TS2742 ×4) and `billing` (`src/db.ts:45` TS2345, the `@types/pg` `Pool` from `/app` vs `/shared`); the other 20 images build cleanly. None of the three is on Platform-S's path, so for the PR #889 gate run I tagged the 28 Sep 08:43 slot-1 images as the slot-4 images for exactly those three and built everything else fresh — recorded on the run so the evidence says which K each service ran.

It is wider than governance. Building every service for a fresh slot one at a time (2026-09-29, `0aa9b52c6`), so far:

* `analytics` — `npm run build`: TS2742 on `app` (`src/index.ts:34`), `router` (`src/routes/analytics.ts:20`), `dashboardRouter` (`src/routes/dashboard.ts:12`), `healthRouter` (`src/routes/health.ts:7`) — all "cannot be named without a reference to `@secuura/shared/node_modules/@types/express-serve-static-core`".
* another service in the same pass — `src/db.ts:45`: TS2345 `import("/app/node_modules/@types/pg").Pool` is not assignable to `import("/shared/node_modules/@types/pg").Pool` — the same shape: `/shared` (built from `packages/shared` inside the image) carries its own `@types/*` that no longer match the service's.
* `nft-certificate` and `transfer` failed once each for a different reason (Docker's disk was full mid-build: `chmod: … No space left on device`); both build after reclaiming space, so they are not part of this.

Two observations for whoever picks it up: (1) the images that exist on this machine from a 28 Sep 08:43 build are fine, and the only 29 Sep commit touching dependencies is KS-1378 (`2cb858335`, morgan / nodemailer / ip-address / undici bumps) — a duplicate-`@types` drift between `packages/shared` and the services is the shape a lockfile bump produces; (2) `Blockchain/Dev/.dockerignore` excludes `node_modules` and `services/*/node_modules` but not `packages/shared/node_modules`, so a host that has run `npm install` inside `packages/shared` would ship that directory into the `COPY packages/shared/ ./` layer — not the case on this machine, but it is a second way to get exactly this error. The full per-service list follows when the loop finishes.
